spec.title: ZAP: Rust runtime, transactional storage, and bounded queries

status.comment: Normative Rust MVP storage contract. The storage engine and precise public API remain architectural and implementation decisions until supported by evidence.

p.RUST-STORAGE-PRODUCTION-LANGUAGE: All ZAP-owned production executable source is Rust, including the domain kernel, transactional application service, storage and index engine, scheduler, protocol validation, CLI, machine backend, and executable adapter helpers. XML, Markdown, JSON, TOML, and English prompts remain data. Python may remain isolated as historical prototype or investigation material, but ordinary build, installation, execution, migration, and verification of the Rust product do not invoke it.

p.RUST-STORAGE-MODULE-BOUNDARIES: The package-owned Cargo workspace separates pure domain transitions, transactional application admission, storage and bounded queries, runtime and effects, host and project adapters, and thin entrypoints. SemanticProvider and AgentHost are distinct. Pure reducers call no clock, network, filesystem, model, worker, or external command. Effects enter through prepared intents and captured observations.

p.RUST-STORAGE-DISTRIBUTABLE-SURFACE: The package declares every code-bearing dependency and installs from its shipped source without a path into the VibeVM source checkout, an undeclared global tool, a committed binary blob, or a Python facade. Stable project capabilities are consumed through published protocols or adapters. An implementation convenience in the host repository is not a distribution contract.

p.RUST-STORAGE-CANONICAL-HISTORY: A StoreId and BaseId bind immutable imported material to an ordered logical event history. Revision, EventId, CommandId, causal predecessors, and reducer or semantic epoch are explicit. An event sequence is semantic authority; exported XML or JSON, materialized indexes, snapshots, GOAL.md, viewer state, and caches are derived and cannot grant authority or replace missing history.

p.RUST-STORAGE-ONE-TRANSACTION: One supported mutation atomically commits one LogicalEvent, its CAS and idempotency receipt, one Sequence and Revision advancement, and every mandatory projection or index mutation needed for safe subsequent admission. A failure commits none of that transition or leaves an explicitly recoverable prepared intent. The storage ADR selects one durability model; independently written files and tables are not described as one atomic operation.

p.RUST-STORAGE-TYPED-REDUCERS: Canonical JSON is limited to validated ingress and immutable event bytes. Domain reducers receive typed payloads and return typed projection mutations; they do not repeatedly parse arbitrary JSON or infer event meaning from strings. Wire validation, canonical byte identity, semantic transition, and storage commit remain explicit seams.

p.RUST-STORAGE-CONTROLLER-FENCE: Exactly one current controller epoch may admit mutations for a campaign. Recovered, duplicated, or stale controllers cannot reuse old admission authority. Idempotency binds one CommandId to one exact payload and result. External effects remain separately reconciled because database atomicity cannot promise exactly-once behavior from an arbitrary host.

p.RUST-STORAGE-LARGE-ARTIFACT-PROTOCOL: Content-addressed large artifacts may live outside transactional rows only through a recoverable publication protocol that binds content identity, committed references, temporary state, final location, and cleanup or repair. A committed reference never silently points to an unpublished object, and an orphan does not become accepted evidence.

p.RUST-STORAGE-MANDATORY-INDEXES: The committed store indexes stable entity identities, hierarchy, typed edges in both directions, source-to-dependent relations, obligation coverage, readiness and blockers, evidence applicability, open encounters, packets and attempts, active claims and effects, holds, and completion blockers. Indexes bind schema, semantic and query versions and committed cursor and are rebuilt or invalidated rather than trusted under an incompatible identity.

p.RUST-STORAGE-INCREMENTAL-INVALIDATION: Known affected views update from changed subjects and reverse dependencies. The runtime does not replay all history, duplicate the whole plan per DreamBranch, scan the complete store for each ordinary command, or eagerly materialize every transitive closure without measurement. Missing semantic edges remain an explicit closure uncertainty that algorithms cannot erase.

p.RUST-STORAGE-BOUNDED-QUERIES: The service supplies revision-bound and paginated node lookup, search, ancestors, dependents, frontier, readiness explanation, affected subgraph, revision comparison, fork reading, packet generation, source detail, why, and attempt resume. Every bounded response states scope, completeness, omitted or unloaded regions, and a continuation cursor. An unvisited region is never returned as an empty or risk-free graph.

p.RUST-STORAGE-SNAPSHOT-TAIL: Snapshots and event tails bind StoreId, BaseId, schema and semantic epoch, reducer and query identity, Revision, last included EventId, and cursor. Duplicate delivery is idempotent; gaps, foreign bases, stale pages, partial final writes, and unsupported versions are explicit. Replay and snapshot-plus-tail projections are required to agree at the same committed boundary.

p.RUST-STORAGE-ALGORITHMIC-NAVIGATION: Graph traversal, deduplication, ordering, reference validation, coverage, blocker counting, source lookup, diffing, and cursor continuation must be bounded Rust operations usable by weak and strong agents and future clients. They do not require loading the complete graph into a model or invoking a model to open a view.

p.RUST-STORAGE-DURABLE-RESUME: Durable state retains charter and outcome revisions, strategic and Lowering lineage, active fork grounds, task contracts, stages and debt, source captures, proof applicability, packets, attempts, claims, DispatchIntents, ExternalJobHandles and receipts, pending effects, holds, safe boundaries, and the next admissible action. A bounded resume projection reconstructs this state after compaction, crash, process or account replacement; it is checked against actual workspace and host observations before action.

p.RUST-STORAGE-UNKNOWN-EFFECT-RECOVERY: Write-ahead intent precedes an external effect. A crash or missing receipt leaves an explicit unknown outcome. Recovery reconciles the bound external identity or postconditions before reissue, preserves attempts and failure classification, and never interprets context loss as permission to reset an approach counter or repeat an effect.

p.RUST-STORAGE-TRUSTED-LOCAL-BOUNDARY: Normal fast reopen may trust crash-safe transactions and a version-bound durable checkpoint only under a documented trusted-local-store boundary in which workers cannot write the store or checkpoint and supported mutation uses the Rust service. Legacy import, explicit distrustful audit, identity mismatch, or deployment without that confinement rederives and validates from canonical history or uses an independent trust anchor. A version label, timestamp, self-hash, or worker promise alone does not establish integrity, and no claim covers a hostile operating-system administrator.

p.RUST-STORAGE-CORRUPTION-REPAIR: Recovery locates the last complete confirmed boundary, preserves corrupt bytes and command ambiguity, and records authorized repair. Middle corruption is not skipped and a partial tail is not treated as completed. While an associated external result is unknown, repair does not authorize repeating it.

p.RUST-STORAGE-EXPLICIT-EPOCH: The Rust store, wire, codec, reducer, and query contracts use explicit version or epoch identities. New stores use StoreEpoch zap/2; read-only legacy import uses LegacyEpoch::Zap1 with domain-separated legacy digests and an explicit identity map. Zap/1 bytes and hashes are not silently reinterpreted under Rust serialization, and package release version remains independently governed.

p.RUST-STORAGE-LOSSLESS-LEGACY-IMPORT: Migration preserves original bytes, identities, order, hierarchy, dependencies, contracts, obligations, evidence, authority classifications, unknown extensions, and legacy digest domains. Codec mapping addresses ordering, escaping, numbers and non-finite values, reserved tags, duplicate members, Unicode, newlines, date and time values, and machine-local paths. Imported state is validated before changing the configured store pointer, and recovery material remains available.

p.RUST-STORAGE-NEXT-INERT: Importing, inspecting, upgrading, installing, or publishing ZAP does not activate the unrelated NEXT campaign. The 425-node and 212-task data set is migration and query evidence only. Current unaccepted prototype candidates retain candidate provenance and cannot become accepted Rust behavior through porting.

p.RUST-STORAGE-GENERIC-PROJECT: ZAP operates in an ordinary VibeVM project through discovered or bound project identity, source handles, package capabilities, user-local context, workspace adapter, toolchain, and verification commands. VibeVM repository paths, Windows paths, pilot IDs, GitHub accounts, and project-specific commands remain fixtures or configuration. Offline, rootless-home, container, and non-GitHub use do not require a central service.

p.RUST-STORAGE-TOTAL-OBSERVABILITY: Versioned machine views expose strategy and execution links, lowering and packet provenance, stages and debt, knowledge and fog, sources, evidence applicability, forks and DreamBranches, costs, role routing, packet composition and omissions, dispatch receipts, liveness, retries, decisions, holds, stop state, completion blockers, invalidation, and repair. Credentials and private sensitive transport data remain excluded. Opening a view performs no semantic reassessment.

p.RUST-STORAGE-TRUTHFUL-CAPABILITIES: Handler, schema, command, query, transport, and adapter registries publish only actually available operations and versions. Unsupported commands and unknown variants are refused. A planned field, fixture, simulated weak transcript, or prototype behavior is not reported as implemented capability.

p.RUST-STORAGE-PERFORMANCE-EVIDENCE: Rust does not by itself prove scale or latency. Declared node, edge, event-history, hardware, cold and warm state, write durability, memory, storage growth, and invalidation fanout accompany performance evidence. Small bounded queries target interactive behavior; long import, audit, rebuild, or large-fanout operations report progress, incomplete results, and resumable boundaries. Proposed numerical targets remain hypotheses until measured.

p.RUST-STORAGE-REFERENCES: Canonical entity and evidence meaning comes from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root. Authority, closure, runtime effects, and public admission come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root and spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUNTIME#root. Agent and packet records come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root.
